name: account
description: Three independent bugs in one file: withdraw rejects an amount equal to the balance (>= should be >), statement numbers entries from 0 (enumerate needs start=1), and transfer calls dst.withdraw instead of dst.deposit (wrong call target). Three tests fail, one per bug; seven pass. The transfer test fails with an exception rather than a wrong value.

name: calendar_utils
description: Three independent bugs in one file: is_leap_year joins its two clauses with `and` instead of `or` (so no year is ever leap), day_of_year subtracts 1 at the end, and parse_iso passes maxsplit=1 to split so a full date never yields three parts. Five tests fail, five pass. Leap-year failures surface both directly and through days_in_month, so localisation must attribute the February failure to is_leap_year.

name: events
description: agenda_line reads event.end_at, but the Event dataclass field is ends_at (AttributeError). The fix renames one attribute access; the receiver's fields are visible in the same file, so a Choice over Event's attributes finds it. Three tests fail (agenda_line twice, agenda once), six pass.

name: grades
description: Two independent one-line bugs in one file: letter_grade uses > where the docstring and tests say boundaries are inclusive (>=), and weighted_average divides by len(weights) instead of sum(weights) (wrong identifier). Three tests fail, seven pass.

name: inventory
description: Two independent one-line bugs in one file: total_value adds qty and price instead of multiplying (operator), and page() treats the 1-based page number as 0-based (off by one). Four tests fail (two per bug), six pass; each bug is exercised by its own tests so the outer loop can fix one failing test at a time.

name: profiles
description: display_name calls .strip() on user.nickname, which is None for users without a nickname (AttributeError). The fix inserts a guard, `if user.nickname is None: return user.full_name`, before the call. Two tests fail (one direct, one through card()), eight pass. short_bio and mask_email in the same file show the None-guard pattern.

name: shipping
description: The free-shipping threshold in the module-level CONFIG dict is 500.0 instead of 50.0, so no test order ever ships free. The fix changes one literal inside the dict; the correct value appears both in the task text and as a literal in the failing tests. Four tests fail, six pass.

name: stats
description: median lacks the empty-sequence guard every sibling has, so median([]) raises IndexError instead of ValueError. The fix inserts `if not values: raise ValueError(...)`. Two tests fail (one direct, one via summary(), which evaluates median first), eight pass. mean/mode/variance directly above show the exact guard to copy.

name: table
description: Two files must change consistently: the helper fmt.pad must gain a `fill` parameter (signature line plus the line that uses it, two hunks in fmt.py) and the caller table.render must pass its own `fill` through to pad (one hunk in table.py). tests/test_fmt.py pins the new helper signature and tests/test_table.py pins the rendered output, so neither file alone suffices; applying only the body hunk in fmt.py breaks every fmt test with a NameError. pad_left in the same file shows the target signature. Four tests fail (two per test file), six pass.

name: tagcloud
description: The module uses collections.Counter in three functions but never imports it; because the annotations are postponed the module imports fine and the NameError only appears when tag_counts/top_tags/co_occurrence run. The fix adds one import line. Four tests fail, five pass.

name: textstats
description: Two independent one-line bugs in one file: most_common sorts ascending because the sorted() call lacks reverse=True (a keyword argument must be added, not swapped), and ngrams drops the last n-gram because its range is short by one. Four tests fail (two per bug), six pass.

name: units
description: Donor-code case: the three-line body of parse_duration is wrong (it slices off the last character as the unit and calls int()), so it cannot handle 'ms', fractions, bare numbers or upper-case units. The sibling parse_size directly above has the correct five-line shape; the fix is to copy it with SIZE_UNITS->DURATION_UNITS and upper()->lower(). One contiguous hunk. Four tests fail, six pass.

name: crossfile
description: Two coordinated one-line edits in two files plus two independent bugs. fmt.money reads its symbol under the wrong option key, options.get(CURRENCY_KEY) for options.get(SYMBOL_KEY) (both module constants of fmt.py; the tests pin `symbol=`), and invoice.render's local `cash` helper builds its options dict under CURRENCY_KEY as well. Either identifier swap alone regresses: fixing the definition makes the fmt tests pass but every invoice line falls back to '$' (two invoice tests break); fixing only the call site changes nothing for fmt and breaks the same two. Only the pair (one patch of two files) is green: test_money_ignores_currency_option pins that the `currency` option is never read as a symbol, so a definition that reads both keys is not a fix either. Independently, tax.tax_for exempts the threshold amount itself (<= for <) and discount.apply_discount negates the percentage-code test (`not in`). Eight tests fail, seventeen pass.

name: import_and_guard
description: Two inserts and two replaces, independent, in four modules. paths.py uses `re` in three functions but never imports it (the annotations are postponed, so the module imports and the NameError appears at call time; one `import re` line at module level, the sibling duration.py has the same line). Settings.get lacks the `if value is None: return default` guard that get_int and get_bool directly below it have, so an unknown key raises AttributeError on None.strip(). retry.schedule iterates range(1, attempts + 1) and yields one delay too many. duration.parse_duration adds the unit size instead of multiplying by it. Twelve tests fail (4 + 2 + 3 + 3), eleven pass.

name: ledger5
description: Pure chain length: five independent one-line bugs in four modules, each with its own failing tests and no shared code paths. isbn10_check_digit weights the digits 9..1 instead of 10..2 (off by one in a constant; breaks the check digit, validation and the ISBN-13 conversion), is_overdue uses >= so a loan is overdue on its due date (operator; also breaks can_renew), fine caps with max() instead of min() (wrong builtin), rank sorts ascending because reverse=False (constant), and label numbers positions from 0 instead of 1 (`number = position` drops the `+ 1`; off by one). Twelve tests fail (3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 2), eighteen pass. The ledger must form and close five goals in sequence without regressing any of them.

name: long_chain
description: A six-stage pipeline with one exception-raising one-line bug per stage; every test of stage N feeds the shared RAW text through stages 1..N, so at the start all sixteen pipeline tests fail with the same ValueError in load.parse_row and form one goal. Fixing stage k lets stage k's tests pass and moves the remaining failures to stage k+1's frame: load.parse_row passes the kind where the price belongs, float(kind) for float(price) (ValueError on the first row), clean_row reads row.label for row.name (AttributeError), to_record indexes LABELS by row.name for row.kind (KeyError), ranked sorts by kv[2] for kv[1] (IndexError), layout.rows calls lines.add for lines.append (AttributeError) and report joins with the undefined SEPARATOR for SEP (NameError). Progress can only come one stage at a time: 16 -> 13 -> 10 -> 6 -> 4 -> 2 -> 0 failing (by_label and grand_total do not go through ranked, so they pass with stage 3). Sixteen tests fail, ten pass (empty-input and helper tests).

name: masked
description: Masking chain: the six report tests all fail at the same NameError in report.summary (`parse_lines(txt)` for `text`). Fixing it makes the two empty-input tests pass; the other four then fail in a callee: those whose log carries durations fail in parse.parse_line (int(took[:-1]) keeps the 'm' of '12ms', ValueError), and every non-empty log fails in aggregate.total_ms (`e.took` for `e.ms`, AttributeError) once parse is fixed, the duration-free logs immediately. The same tests must be re-clustered twice as their traceback frame moves report -> parse -> aggregate; the direct parse and aggregate tests never exercise the two callee paths (durations, non-empty totals). Six tests fail, sixteen pass.

name: regress_trap
description: Regressions must never be kept. Bug 1: agenda.Item.span returns (first_day, last_day) instead of (first_day, last_day + 1), so items vanish on their last day and never clash; the obvious mutations, `<` -> `<=` in intervals.contains or in intervals.overlaps, make the agenda tests pass but break the pinned half-open semantics in tests/test_intervals.py and tests/test_slots.py (end minute free, touching slots bookable). The fix is the off-by-one at the span line. Bug 2 has the same shape: roster.badge slices one initial instead of two, and shortening names.initials would pass the badge tests while breaking test_names. Bugs 3 and 4 are plain: intervals.merge does not merge touching intervals (< for <=) and names.surname returns the first word (parts[0] for parts[-1]). Seven tests fail, twenty-one pass.

name: shared_frame
description: The `account` partial trap by construction: two bugs in two different modules whose failing tests all raise InvalidValue at the same line of the shared helper checks.ensure_at_least, so frame clustering merges them into one goal. booking.reserve demands at least 1 remaining seat instead of 0 (constant; two tests), and pricing.total swaps the arguments of ensure_at_least(seats, 1, ...) so any order of two or more seats is rejected (argument swap; four tests). Each correct fix alone makes only its own tests pass and is therefore a partial of the merged goal; the two partials have disjoint newly-passing sets and must be paired or committed as partials. checks.py's own tests pin `<` in the helper, so mutating the shared line regresses them. Six tests fail, nineteen pass.

name: six_hunks
description: Six data-dependent one-line bugs in five modules, caught only by three parametrised integration tests in one shared file; the per-module tests cover the unaffected inputs and pass. Each integration test has three cases that depend on a pair of bugs: `a_only` fails for the first bug alone, `b_only` for the second alone, `both` for either, so every goal (one per test function) holds two complementary partials and closes only when both fixes are in. test_attention: Task.is_overdue counts a task due today (<= for <) and filters.due_within drops the last day of the window (< for <=). test_board: sorting.by_due puts undated tasks first (`is not None` for `is None`) and render.line keeps one character too many before the '...' (width - 2 for width - 3). test_summary: stats.completion_rate floors (// for /) and average_priority rounds to 0 decimals instead of 1. Nine tests fail, twenty pass.
